title: 6 weeks until mocks – your weekly plan
caption: Mocks in 6 weeks? Here's the whole plan, week by week. Screenshot it, stick it on your wall, thank yourself in January 📅

slides.headline: {6 weeks} until mocks
slides.sub: Your week-by-week plan. Screenshot it. Stick it on your wall.

slides.headline: Traffic-light {every topic}
slides.body: List every topic in every subject. Rate each red, amber or green. Be brutally honest.

slides.headline: Close the book, {write it out}
slides.body: Learn a red topic, then write down everything you remember. Testing beats rereading a week later.

slides.headline: One past paper {per subject}
slides.body: Timed, then marked. Every lost mark goes on next week's to-do list.

slides.headline: Go back to {week 1–2} topics
slides.body: Returning after a gap makes it stick. That's spacing, and it's one of the best-evidenced techniques.

slides.headline: Full papers, {real timings}
slides.body: Short daily recall. No all-nighters: experts recommend 8–10 hours' sleep for 13–18 year olds.

slides.headline: Your countdown, {sorted}
slides.body: Plasmo counts down to your mocks and marks your past-paper answers as you go.

sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning (Psychological Science, 2006) – APS Observer summary
sources.claim: Students who took recall tests retained substantially more after 2 days and 1 week than students who restudied, although restudying won at 5 minutes and made students more confident.

sources.title: Spacing effects in learning: a temporal ridgeline of optimal retention
sources.claim: Spacing study sessions improves retention; the optimal gap grows with the retention interval.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques – press summary
sources.claim: Distributed practice and practice testing were the two techniques rated high utility.

sources.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for Pediatric Populations: AASM consensus statement
sources.claim: Teenagers 13–18 years should sleep 8 to 10 hours per 24 hours on a regular basis.

sources.title: Plasmo – past papers, marked by AI
sources.claim: Past papers answered online and marked straight away. (Mock countdown feature: confirm from the app screenshot.)
